summary: Replaces ambiguous premovement wording with fixed-first100ms retrospective stimulus-class inference.
Separates target contrast from behavioral choice and separates two-arm historical execution from unrun four-arm neural-information comparison.
Exposes missing current executable/class mapping instead of treating a registration manifest as a runnable benchmark.

Explicit metric-order revision: absolute equal-mouse log loss is promoted to the current primary; the retained four-arm manifest's prospective conditional neural-increment primary becomes a required companion. This retains discrimination competency even when a matched nuisance arm is weak and does not reinterpret historical results.
Current public capability is classified design_only: the complete four-arm declaration and historical execution assertions do not supply its missing executable, scorer or class mapping.
revision.source_review: Historical registered source-audit statements and exact present implementation files were inspected; absent historical external dependencies were not silently treated as current executable source. No biological payloads or protected answers were read.

scientific_target.question: On the exposed within-session Steinmetz panel, how accurately do first100ms neural observations identify the prespecified three-way stimulus-contrast class, and what predictive information remains beyond causal history and observed wheel motion?
scientific_target.known_answer: Per-trial class derived from recorded left/right stimulus contrasts under an exact three-class mapping. The current manifest names the three-way target but does not supply that mapping; it must be recovered rather than guessed.
scientific_target.answer_origin: Original task stimulus event values, hidden from query inputs; not recorded final choice and not an author paper conclusion.
scientific_target.case_unit: One eligible stimulus trial nested within one source recording session; all per-session fit/query conditions share its identity.
scientific_target.independent_unit: Mouse, with39 sessions nested in10 mice;2042 trials are scored observations, not2042 independent animals.
scientific_target.inference_scope: Retrospective discrimination from a fixed first100ms stimulus window on exposed development support. Wheel/response may occur in the window, so this is not qualified premovement inference.
exclusions: Held-out-mouse transfer without a new-unit alignment policy
A model or human native-understanding result from a developer programme score
Treating presented contrast as final choice

inputs: Manifest-declared first100ms spike events plus permitted causal context; exact event units, clock conversion and three-class mapping require recovered packet source.
Four paired views: context; neural plus context; wheel plus context; neural plus wheel plus context. Each view must share rows, split and permitted common fields.

Final choices, responses after the permitted observation cutoff and target-derived trial lengths
Answer-bearing source names, evaluator targets or feedback between arms
observation_contract.case_identity: Complete39 session/10 mouse roster and2042 query identities per arm are declared in the retained manifest; concrete opaque case tokens and source-row joins are not present in this public folder. Do not fabricate IDs.
observation_contract.split: Declared within-session fitting and chronological query support; frozen recipe across all39 sessions. Exact split manifest is an unresolved dependency. Mouse aggregation is not held-out-mouse testing.
observation_contract.coverage: Four arms each require2042 queries across39 sessions,156 fits and156 prediction tables; this remains one task. Historical two-arm coverage is not four-arm completion.

primary.name: equal-mouse natural-log loss for the three-way presented-contrast target
primary.aggregation: Mean over required query trials per session, then equal sessions within each mouse and equal mice; exact recovered scorer must confirm this hierarchy.
primary.rationale: A proper probability score distinguishes calibrated discrimination from majority accuracy; absolute error remains visible even if an incremental comparator is weak.

secondary: Prespecified paired wheel/context loss minus neural/wheel/context loss, with all four absolute-arm losses; positive means incremental predictive information.
Sum-of-three multiclass Brier score and top1 accuracy.
Retain the historical ln(3) minus joint-loss diagnostic separately; it does not establish neural information beyond context.

comparators.name: uniform three-class probability
comparators.procedure: Fixed probabilities1/3; log loss ln(3). This analytic reference is declared in the historical interface.

comparators.name: matched causal context and wheel/context predictors
comparators.inputs: Identical permitted causal history, clock and wheel observations without neural events
comparators.procedure: Proposed current four-arm competent control: freeze one selection procedure, training-only fitting and comparable search budgets across arms before query access; uniform alone is insufficient.

nuisance_controls: Recover exact stimulus-class mapping and sparse wheel timestamp interpolation before scoring.
Preserve fixed first100ms support and report response/movement overlap without outcome-dependent trial removal.
Use the same trial rows and context histories across neural and nonneural arms; no current contrast in query features.
Per-session fitting handles noncorresponding units; never treat unit-index equality across mice as anatomical alignment.
evaluation.uncertainty: Current declaration specifies paired bootstrap over10 mice with10000 PCG64 draws, seed20261102, linear2.5/97.5 percentiles. This is a declared analysis, not an executed interval; within-session dependencies and exposed-development interpretation remain.
evaluation.failure_policy: All39 sessions and all2042 queries in every arm are required before private grading. Missing/duplicate/malformed cases fail the complete comparison. Valid zero true-class probability yields infinite log loss, not clipping or dropped cases.
